name: effect-fence-node-sibling-does-not-implement-404
description: R10 -- THE ASYMMETRY, RECORDED. The sibling Node coordinator does not implement /hooks/effect-fence and answers 404 with the shared {error: <lowercase phrase>} envelope. This is the deliberate state, not a gap to close silently: an unimplemented route is a VISIBLE gap, whereas two coordinators disagreeing about whether an irreversible effect may fire is a silent one, so a Node implementation that drifts from the Python branch table would be worse than none. The bearer is VALID (the harness supplies it on every request) because the Node coordinator rejects auth BEFORE routing -- with a bad or missing bearer this request answers 401 and the 404 would say nothing about which routes exist. The day Node grows the route, this fixture goes red and someone decides whether the two implementations agree leg for leg. Its row must RUN, not skip: test_effect_fence_corpus.py fails rather than xfails when the plugin dist cannot be resolved, because a green-by-skip is exactly how a cross-implementation claim stops being checked.
_comment: Node-only row, following warn_mode/11-health-node-only.json. No ignore_keys: the 404 envelope carries a single constant phrase and no timestamp, uptime, pid, port or epoch-shaped value, so nothing here needs normalization -- test_effect_fence_corpus.py asserts that property across the whole fixture set rather than leaving it to a reader.
